title: Coach catalog
goal: Fill a coordinator's group: see which AI/Run coaches have no coordinator, judge them against how this coordinator actually works, take ten, and open the group chat with them.
primaryQuestion: Which free coach is worth taking?

zones.name: header
zones.purpose: Name the screen and carry its ONE page-level action — as a SECONDARY button, because when unpushed picks exist the notice zone's write-the-workbook button appears on the same surface and that one is the answer of the moment; two filled buttons side by side is a screen answering twice. The Refresh button is gone (2026-08-17): the page already re-read the local copy on open, so the button only decided WHEN to go and fetch the workbook, which is not a decision a coordinator should make — `useFreshSot` tops it up in the background when the copy is over an hour old. What is left opens the group chat with everyone taken so far, and is disabled with a Tooltip saying why while nobody is taken — the pick and the message are one job, and sending it from a different screen would mean carrying a list of names across a navigation.

zones.name: toolbar
zones.purpose: Everything that narrows 116 coaches, in one row of equal-height controls: search by name, email or location; the Free / Mine / All switch carrying its counts, because the default view hides the 78 coaches another coordinator already has and saying so is what keeps the screen from reading as broken; then one dropdown per facet of the Coaches tab — language, region, wave, confirmed, teams carried. Search renders EXPANDED: it is the fastest way to a name and hiding it behind a click costs a click on every visit. Under the row, on a line of its own: how many of the ten are taken, how many rows match, what the view is hiding, and how old the workbook is.

zones.name: content
zones.answers: Which free coach is worth taking?
zones.purpose: One card per coach: name and location, the fit score with its verdict, the two or three reasons behind it, timezone, wave, languages, the tools they say they have used, how many teams they carry against their target, and what KIND of work they do — the internal-product track the workbook puts on the PERSON (the wave cell spelled "3 (IPP)", or a row on the IPP Coaches sheet), and beside it whether the teams they carry are internal company products or client ones. Two facts on one line, because neither follows from the other: 15 coaches carry an internal product and 5 are internal-product coaches. It is the same mark the team cards carry per team, and nothing on this card used to say which was which. The score is PERSONAL to the coordinator reading it — hours their working days overlap, a coaching language they share beyond English, tools this coordinator has used, whether the coach has confirmed and whether they wrote a real answer about their own agentic workflow — so the reasons are sentences about this pair, not about the coach in the abstract. A coach another coordinator has, or one the workbook parks on hold, keeps the same card without the take button and says who has them. A coach this coordinator let go keeps their card with the date and the reason. The grid is a container query in the page CSS, so the column count follows the content column rather than the viewport, and it grows in batches as it is scrolled rather than paging. The WHOLE CARD opens the coach detail the programme view ALREADY has — their teams, their load, what they wrote about their own practice — rather than a second detail screen about the same person, which would be two truths to keep in step. The title control carries `card-link`, whose ::after covers the tile, so the hit area is the card while there is still one accessible name and one focus stop; `Card interactive` supplies the cursor and the hover lift. The actions row and the flag row carry `card-above`, so taking a coach and reading a language name still work over that layer. The Saved segment is the same shortlist the team catalog has, keyed by coach name: a coordinator marks candidates, writes down why, thinks, and only then takes from the basket — with reserves left in it for when somebody drops out. Saving touches no workbook and no chat; a pick or a release clears the candidate. The card is four blocks with a hairline between them — who they are, what they carry, why this score, what you can do — and each block answers one question: eleven rows of equal weight made three cards side by side read as one. The score is said ONCE, as the badge; the full-width bar under it could not tell 90 from 85 to any eye that read it, so it was decoration on every card. Reasons the card has already stated are dropped rather than repeated (every free coach used to lead with "No coordinator yet", which is the definition of the segment). Keeping a coach is an icon-only star with a Tooltip — a filled star says "saved" and the word beside it said nothing more — and the note is edited by clicking the note itself rather than by a second button. Turning a coach down is a named item in a small menu, not a bare cross beside the primary button, which read as "hide this card". The card lives in apps/airun/src/components/coordinator/CoachCard.tsx; the team catalog's card follows the same grammar. The card carries TWO icon actions and nothing else: the star keeps a candidate, the second one takes them (or undoes a take). A filled blue button on every card made a list of cards read as a list of forms, and the menu behind it held one item. Turning a free row down with a reason is gone from this screen entirely — nobody was doing it here, and the cross that carried it read as "hide this card". The name is a HEADING, one step larger than the body and not painted or underlined as a link: the whole card is the link, and a link inside a link-shaped card is two hit areas for one thing. The reasons sit under a "Why this fit" label, because loose sentences under a row of facts do not say what they are or who they are about. The facts inside a card sit in a <Row>, never in <CardMeta>: CardMeta is the card's FOOTER here — it draws its own hairline, pins itself to the bottom and pushes its items to both edges, which put a second divider in the middle of the card and scattered four facts across its width. The score badge sits on the same LINE as the name, not centred against the name plus the line under it, where it was beside neither. A bullet under "Why this fit" that repeats a fact printed two lines above it is dropped at the source (size, brief grade, availability): of three bullets, two used to be facts already on the card.

zones.name: notice
zones.purpose: The page-level fact that outranks the list when it exists: picks and releases not yet written to the workbook list themselves by name in a warning Alert whose button does the write, spelled as the sentence it will write — the same rule as the team catalog's. Conditional: a coordinator with nothing pending never sees it.

zones.name: dialogs
zones.purpose: The two writes this screen performs against the local roster. Taking a coach is a confirmation, because it is a claim other coordinators will see once the workbook catches up and until then it is local. Letting one go is a form, because the reason is the payload the programme leads read as a signal.

zones.name: outreach
zones.purpose: The group chat with everyone taken so far, opened by a header button and living in its own component (apps/airun/src/components/coordinator/MenteesOutreach.tsx) because it is a self-contained job with its own sign-in state: a Modal composing Field, Input, Textarea, Chip, SectionLabel, Stack and Row. One group chat for all of them rather than ten private ones, because they are becoming one working group and the introduction is the same for everybody. The message is English, the programme's language and the one language every coach on the tab lists, and it is editable before it is sent — it goes to real people over Microsoft Graph, so nothing is sent that has not been read. The modal states plainly whether Microsoft is signed in and offers the sign-in when it is not. The button appears only once at least one coach is taken: a chat with nobody in it is not an action.

states.loading: Six Skeleton shape=block cards in the grid under a single aria-busy on the grid element. The read is a local file and a scored pass over 116 rows, so this is short; it exists so the quota line does not sit above an empty page.
states.empty: EmptyState through the template's empty prop, two cases kept apart: reason='no-matches' with icon=tune when the filters emptied the list, offering to clear them; reason='no-data' with icon=group when the workbook holds no coach without a coordinator, offering Refresh.
states.error: Alert tone=danger above the grid when the catalog could not be read — no workbook pulled yet, or the bridge is not running — naming what it looked for and offering Refresh. An unread list is not an empty list, so this is not the empty state.
states.noPermission: Alert tone=info in place of the grid when the signed-in coach is not named on the workbook's Coordinators sheet: the screen still lists the coaches, and every take button is gone, because picking coaches is a coordinator's job and the tool has no way to make somebody one. It is a ROLE the workbook states, not an access control this app enforces, and the copy says exactly that instead of implying a permission system.

data: coaches: name, email, wave, location, timezone, utcOffset, languages, tools, sdlcStages, teamsTarget, confirmed, workflow, coordinator — coach/sources/coaches-sot.json, converted from the AI/Run workbook's Coaches tab (116 rows on this machine: 28 with no coordinator, 78 taken, 10 on hold)
coordinators: name and how many coaches they carry — the workbook's Coordinators sheet. Being named there is what makes the take buttons appear, and it is where the target of ten comes from.
load per coach: how many teams the Teams tab assigns them, plus the IPP sheet, against the target in their own row — coach/sources/teams-sot.json

fit: score 0-100, verdict (strong | possible | weak), reasons[], flags[] — tools/lib/coach-fit.mjs, the coordinator-side twin of the team rubric in tools/lib/fit.mjs, scoring the coordinator-to-coach pair rather than the coach-to-team one

picks and releases: written into the workbook's Coordinator column (Coaches!M{row}) through the Excel REST API, then appended to coach/events/mentees.jsonl in the same append-only shape the team roster uses. The workbook is written FIRST and is the authority: a coach it already gives to another coordinator is refused, not recorded here. Every write is guarded (the row's Name cell must still hold the coach we mean, the target cell must be empty or ours), read back, and logged to coach/events/sot-writes.jsonl with its before and after values.

the group chat: coach/mentees/outreach.json holds the chat name, the message and the chat id once Microsoft Graph has created it, so a reload keeps the draft and the weekly follow-up can post into the same chat instead of scanning every group chat by topic
openQuestions: Whether the programme leads want the Coordinators tally sheet kept in step as well. The tool writes the Coordinator column on the Coaches tab, which is the fact; the small tally beside it (name, how many coaches) is derived from that column and is left to whoever owns it, because two writers of one number is how a number stops being trusted.

What a coordinator should see when their name is REMOVED from a coach by somebody else. The card flips back to free on the next Refresh, which is correct and silent; whether that deserves a notice depends on how often the leads reshuffle, and nobody has the numbers yet.

behaviours.given: a coordinator releasing a coach from their group
behaviours.when: the release reason is about this group (not responding, no capacity)
behaviours.then: the coach's teams STAY theirs; only leaving the programme frees the rows
behaviours.why: Two of three released coaches were picked up by another coordinator within days while holding five teams each.
